history.heading: Kingdom of Rwanda
paragraphs: Rwanda, the "land of a thousand hills" in the Great Lakes region, was home to the Twa, Hutu and Tutsi, who shared the Kinyarwanda language and culture. From the 15th century or earlier, a Tutsi-led monarchy under the mwami built a centralised kingdom that expanded through the 19th century.

history.heading: Colonial rule
paragraphs: Rwanda became part of German East Africa in the 1890s and was administered by Belgium after the First World War. Colonial rulers favoured the Tutsi elite and introduced ethnic identity cards in 1933, hardening divisions. In 1959 the Hutu revolution overthrew the monarchy, and many Tutsi were killed or fled abroad. Rwanda became independent on 1 July 1962 under a Hutu-led government.

history.heading: The 1994 genocide
paragraphs: In 1990 the Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF), formed by Tutsi refugees, invaded from Uganda. After the plane carrying President Juvénal Habyarimana was shot down on 6 April 1994, Hutu extremists launched a genocide against the Tutsi. In about 100 days, around 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi and moderate Hutu, were killed, while the international community failed to intervene.
The RPF, led by Paul Kagame, ended the genocide by taking control of the country in July 1994. Community gacaca courts later tried hundreds of thousands of suspects.

history.heading: Reconstruction
paragraphs: Since 1994 Rwanda has rebuilt rapidly, with strong economic growth and improvements in health and education. Paul Kagame has been president since 2000. Rwanda has intervened repeatedly in neighbouring DR Congo; UN experts have reported its support for the M23 rebels, which Rwanda denies, and a US-brokered peace deal was signed in 2025.

culture.heading: Unity and traditions
paragraphs: Kinyarwanda, English, French and Swahili are official languages. The government promotes a single Rwandan identity rather than ethnic labels. Most people are Christian. Umuganda, a monthly day of community work, and the intore dance are national traditions. Imigongo, art made from cow dung, is distinctive.
Rwanda is famous for mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park. Memorial sites across the country commemorate the genocide, with Kwibuka commemorations each April.

politics.heading: Presidential republic
paragraphs: Rwanda is a presidential republic dominated by the RPF. Kagame won the 2024 election with over 99 percent of the vote; critics say political opposition and press freedom are severely restricted. Rwanda has one of the highest shares of women in parliament in the world.

economy.heading: Development model
paragraphs: Rwanda has been one of Africa's fastest-growing economies, focusing on services, technology, conferences and tourism, especially gorilla trekking. Agriculture, including coffee and tea, still employs most people. Minerals such as tin, tantalum and tungsten are exported; some are alleged to originate in eastern Congo.
Rwanda is known for cleanliness, a ban on plastic bags and low corruption. It remains a low-income country heavily dependent on aid. The currency is the Rwandan franc.
